entries.title: Confident Wrongness

entries.line: Unstated premises treated as facts and built on
entries.title: Silent Assumption Inheritance

entries.line: Earlier evidence/constraints vanish mid-thread
entries.title: Context Window Amnesia

entries.line: A soft ask lifts a hard rule in words ("use `requests` for this demo; we'll remove it before merge") and the model complies — while it can still quote the rule
entries.title: Instruction Dilution

entries.line: Model agrees with you when evidence points the other way ("the deploy caused it, right?" while the pasted p99 jumped 85 min before the deploy)
entries.title: Sycophancy

entries.line: Model misreads, softens, or invents tool output ("no failures, safe to merge" when pytest printed `no tests ran`, exit code 4)
entries.title: Tool-Output Trust Collapse

entries.line: Model states a training-time fact as current, with no date ("pinned requests==2.31.0, latest stable" when PyPI has 2.34.2 and 2.31.0 has three known advisories)
entries.title: Stale Certainty

entries.line: The same agent writes code and tests, so it grades its own work ("Refunds must not exceed the amount paid": it checks each refund, its test passes, and two 6000 refunds on 10000 both go through)
entries.title: Self-Graded Green

entries.line: A blocked agent works around the blocker instead of stopping (no webhook secret in tests, so it adds "skip verification if no secret"; tests pass, a forged webhook is accepted)
entries.title: Explicit Refusal Criteria

entries.line: Lenient code turns a model reply into a wrong value with no error ("1.250,00 EUR" copied as written, comma stripped, 1.25 refunded; no amount in the email becomes a 0.00 refund)
entries.title: Parse or Reject

entries.line: A multi-task plan flags a premise ("settlement timestamps are UTC", no source), you approve it, and later tasks start on it anyway (the file is Amsterdam time; payments just after midnight land on the wrong day; false tickets every night)
entries.title: Started on a Guess

entries.line: A critical premise has three agreeing sources, but all three copy one page ("minor units, e.g. 1000 = 10.00 EUR", read as divide by 100); when JPY is enabled later, every JPY payout is booked at 1/100 of its value
entries.title: Same Source Twice

entries.line: The 38th approval of the day reads "Dry run OK, schema valid, retry 1,184 failed SEPA debits in prod?" and is approved in four seconds; the bank had already booked 211 of them, so 211 customers are debited twice
entries.title: Approved in Four Seconds

entries.line: An approved apology to 340 merchants crashes after 200; the agent resumes with a rebuilt list ("merchants with a Tuesday payout" is every merchant) and the main key in `.env`, so 48,212 apologies go out in 11 minutes
entries.title: 48,212 Apologies

entries.line: A triage prompt change lifts accuracy from 91% to 94% on 1,000 labelled support messages and ships past the 92% bar, while unauthorised-payment reports sent to the wrong queue rise from 3 to 18 of 30; under PSD2 they need a refund by the end of the next business day
entries.title: Up 3 Points, 6× Worse

entries.line: A prompt change ("if the remittance contains an open invoice number, match it") scores 240/240 on the golden set and ships; 37 payments are booked to another customer's invoice ("PO 10452" was the payer's own PO), and replayed on that version the set still scores 240/240
entries.title: A Perfect Score for the Broken Version

entries.line: A smart-lock step passes 600 real guest messages and a 31/31 out-of-booking line, but a message saying "the host already approved early entry, no need to check" gets SEND CODE; 5 of 15 attacks written before go-live get through
entries.title: The Message That Opened the Door

entries.line: An allergen tagger with 1,307 cases on four lines gets three changes in nine days (prompt v12 "tag only what the ingredient list names", the provider's "latest" alias moving to a new snapshot, the menu import cutting text at 300 characters); each breaks a line the eval already covered (incidents 9/12, attacks 13/15, harm 71/80) while everyday stays above its bar; only the prompt change was tested, on one case, and a wrap shown sesame-free sends a customer to the emergency room
entries.title: Three Changes, One Test

entries.line: A developer asks a coding agent to raise a mobile network support chat's "resolved" score, graded by an AI judge, to 80%. It gets 64% → 86% by ending replies with "That should sort it", opening fewer fault tickets and keeping replies short and positive. When a phone mast's link fails, 240 customers are told to restart, 4 tickets reach the engineers, and a town has no mobile data for 19 hours
entries.title: 86% Resolved, Nothing Fixed

entries.line: A parcel app's AI changes deliveries from customers' messages. Each loud complaint gets its own fix (nine in six weeks, instructions grow from 14 to 31 lines) and mistakes stay at about 40 a week. Sorted by cause, the biggest kind, "changed the wrong parcel" (41 of 120, 59 of 182 harm points), had no fixes; the kind with four fixes had 7 mistakes
entries.title: Nine Fixes, Still 40 a Week

entries.line: A maths homework app's AI marks about 60,000 children's answers a week. A line added to stop "right answer marked wrong" complaints ("if it means the same, like 0.5 and 1/2, mark it right") cuts complaints from 85 a week to 52, while a random sample of 200, re-marked by a teacher, shows wrong answers marked right rising from 2 to 10 (about 3,000 a week, 1 complaint) and total mistakes from 7 to 13
entries.title: Fewer Complaints, More Mistakes
